answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with adaptive compute pricing: every new identity must burn a small, rising amount of verifiable work before it can transact, like paying a toll at a wharf that grows steeper the more identities arrive from the same grove of machines. A lone honest agent pays a trivial cost, but an attacker spinning up thousands of clones faces a bill that scales faster than any profit, while the velvet-smooth onboarding honest users enjoy stays intact because the fee stays tiny for a single real identity.
